title: Trades Power for Convenience
text:
Trades Power for Convenience. My wife has been after me for a vacuum cleaner like this that is small, lightweight and is easy to handle. I selected this one for her and we spent an evening testing it out and putting it through its paces. It has some excellent qualities but we were both disappointed with it in several areas.

Taking this fellow out of the box, it comes disassembled to save space in shipping. Assembly took less than 5 minutes, and most of the time spent was taking the parts out of the box and getting them out of the protective plastic. That was a good sign right off the bat.

This is an extremely lightweight unit, even with the battery installed. It is definitely easy to handle and that’s excellent for her, as she doesn’t like pushing around our heavy Dyson. When it’s broken down and being used as a small convenience vacuum, such as for doing the stairs or working in the car it is even more lightweight. This one gets high marks for the size and weight.

Our first task for this vacuum was the linoleum kitchen floor, and it did a fantastic job with it. We ran it on low power, and it managed to pick up almost everything, the exceptions being things that were stuck down and had to be scraped from the floor. Because of the size and the swivel action of the head, it is super easy to maneuver around corners, along the cabinetry and under chairs and tables. We kicked on the “turbo” mode and it didn’t seem to make any difference in this scenario – not a big deal, just a data point. Even when on full power, we were pleased with how quiet this vacuum cleaner is compared to our corded upright.

We moved over to the carpet and hit a high-traffic area, and as we predicted it did a fair job but not as good a job as our Dyson. I expected that a battery-powered vacuum would trade the convenience for power, and I was right, though it did well enough to pick up most visible debris from the carpet.

Where this vacuum really showed its compromise in power, though, was when we decided to clean cat hair from the couch. We have two cats, and they love our cloth-covered couch, so there’s plenty of hair to vacuum away on any given day. We converted the vacuum to a handheld, attached the upholstery head, put it on high power and proceeded to vacuum the couch cushions. It did a fair job, but it left as much as it collected and we reverted to a different vacuum to finish the job.

When finished, we emptied the collection bin, and this proved to be the easiest vacuum to empty of any we have used. Press a button on the side to pop open the canister door, and simply dump out the contents into a plastic bag. It doesn’t require partial disassembly or anything. It is smaller than most, of course, so it will not collect as much.

We ran the battery completely out of power and plugged it in to charge. It literally took 5 hours to go from completely empty to fully-charged. That’s a lot of time to charge the battery, to get 30-45 minutes of run time! That requires some planning ahead when using this unit. In light of this, I looked into getting a second battery, and was startled to find that batteries are presently selling for $100. That’s 1/3 the cost of the vacuum itself. I was hoping the battery would instead cost $50-$60, which to me is a reasonable cost. On the plus side, the battery does not need to be in the vacuum cleaner itself to be charged.

This vacuum cleaner is an interesting unit. It has some excellent qualities, among them being size and weight and the ability to convert to a hand-held with no cord, but it has some downsides too, such as the battery cost and the lack of power in certain circumstances. I can’t say this is a bad unit, but consider how you’d use it: if you’ll be using it on hardwood or linoleum, it’s really great, but if you want to use it on carpet of furniture it struggles to perform. Also weigh the cost/convenience of buying a second battery – it’s an appreciable chunk of money for a fairly short runtime.

features: Powerful cordless suction for everyday dirt, debris, and high-traffic areas
Up to 40 minutes of runtime in handheld vacuum power mode. Includes a removable battery, which can be charged in or out of the cordless vacuum.
DuoClean Technology invented for fine dust and large debris on carpets and hard floors. One powerhead, two brushrolls.
Up to 30 minutes of runtime for hard floor cleaning and 25 minutes of runtime for carpet cleaning in ION Power mode.
Transforms to a hand vacuum for lightweight handheld cleaning in hard-to-reach places, above the floor, and in the car.
